title: SDLC
body:
[[Models]]

**Software Development Life Cycle.** The five phases every software project passes through,
whatever process model is wrapped around them:

1. **Requirements** what the system has to do. See [[Software Requirements Analysis]].
2. **Design** how it will be built. See [[Design]], [[Structured Approach]],
   [[Object Oriented Approach]].
3. **Implementation** writing it.
4. **Testing** checking it, from [[Unit testing]] up to the system as a whole.
5. **Maintenance** everything after release: fixes, changes, and the reason
   [[Coupling and Cohesion]] matters at all.

The phases are the same in every model. What differs is the *order and repetition*:
[[Waterfall]] runs them once in sequence, [[Agile]] runs all five inside every iteration.
That is the whole distinction, and [[Models]] is where it lives.

The fact worth carrying out of this course: **the cost of fixing a defect rises sharply the
later in the cycle it is found.** A misunderstood requirement caught during analysis is a
conversation; the same one caught in maintenance is a rewrite of everything built on top of
it. Every process argument in software engineering is ultimately an argument about how to
find things earlier.

Maintenance is also the phase that consumes the most effort over a system's life, which is
the reverse of how much attention it gets in the [[Design]] phase.
